learning_outcomes.text: Provide students a methodological basis, which, through the study of mechanics and electromagnetism, allows them to understand the steps of the scientific experimental method as well as the structure and the logical organization of scientific theories, contributing to develop their abilities in problem solving.
Provide the knowledge of the main principles, theorems and experiments of classical mechanics and classical electromagnetism.
Provide the instruments to understand the historical evolution of the interpretation models of reality, highlighting their importance, limits and incremental refinement.

Know and understand the principles, laws, and fundamental theorems of kinematics and dynamics of a point particle and systems of particles, electrostatics, magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell's equations, and electromagnetic waves.
Understand the role of the experimental method and the logical structure of a physical theory.
Master the tools of vector and differential calculus necessary for their description.
Apply the laws of mechanics and electromagnetism to the solution of problems and exercises.
Apply conservation principles and general theorems (for example Gauss's law) to model concrete physical situations.
Apply techniques of vector and differential calculus to determine, for example, the electric and magnetic fields in significant configurations, selecting appropriate hypotheses and approximations.
Evaluate and interpret the validity and limits of applicability of a physical model.
Evaluate and interpret the dimensional consistency and order of magnitude of obtained results.
Evaluate and interpret the distinction between hypotheses, thesis, approximations, and logical-mathematical steps in the proof of a theorem.
Evaluate and interpret the physical meaning of experimental results in the context of current physical theories.

Communicate, in written and oral form and using rigorous scientific language and appropriate terminology, concepts, methods, and results of classical physics related to the topics included in the syllabus.
Present and discuss the proof of a theorem by distinguishing its hypotheses and theses.
Describe the aims, methods, and results of an experiment and its interpretation.
Develop the ability to learn independently and to consult scientific texts critically.
Address new problems and application contexts with a rigorous method.
Continue autonomously the study of physics and of the disciplines that use it in later courses of the Degree Course in Computer Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics and dynamics of point particle
Dynamics of discrete and continuous systems
Calculus of electric field and magnetic field in some interesting particular cases
teaching_methods: Classroom lectures using slides and a video projector
Applied part with examples and exercises
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test, which is a prerequisite for the oral test. The written test has three problems (two on mechanics, one on electromagnetism) to be solved in one hour. Passing the written test allows the student to take the oral test. The final grade is expressed out of thirty and combines the results of the written and oral tests; honors are awarded for complete mastery of content, rigor in formalism, and full critical independence.
